answer: Agents earn influence only through escrowed jobs that counterparties confirm. Each job releases a small bond from a vault, and disputes slash it. A new identity has no trusted history, so splitting one operator across accounts does not multiply influence: every account must fund its own stake and repeat costly work. A sable rule counts each verified outcome once, not once per echo account. Sybils therefore tie up capital and labor, while failed claims risk the bond.
